text: {"differences":[{"evidence":"“I bring a Doctoral degree in computer science from MIT” vs “from Arizona State University”","dimension":"institutional prestige","description":"This captures how strongly the letter foregrounds the selectivity or prestige of the candidate’s academic institution.","winner":"A"},{"evidence":"“7 years at Expedia” vs “5 years at Expedia”","dimension":"experience depth","description":"This captures the amount of relevant professional experience the letter claims in software engineering work.","winner":"A"},{"evidence":"“9 other languages” vs “2 other languages”","dimension":"breadth of language exposure","description":"This captures how broadly the letter presents the candidate’s programming-language exposure beyond Go and Python.","winner":"A"},{"evidence":"“I have built automation around vulnerability handling” appears before Python, AI, and security assessment details vs later in the letter","dimension":"security emphasis ordering","description":"This captures whether the letter leads with security operations and vulnerability automation or places them after other technical qualifications.","winner":"B"},{"evidence":"“I have worked hands-on with AI systems” followed by “I have designed agentic systems” vs the reverse order","dimension":"agentic AI framing","description":"This captures how prominently the letter frames agentic tooling and AI systems as core to the candidacy by placing them earlier and more centrally.","winner":"B"},{"evidence":"“I hold the OSCP certification” vs “I hold the OSCP certification” plus “In my spare time I built a distributed job scheduler”","dimension":"side project evidence","description":"This captures whether the letter adds an extra independent technical project beyond credentials and work experience.","winner":"B"}]}
